race_context: The district: Prairie Heights Community School Corporation, which has a LaGrange mailing address, serves parts of LaGrange and Steuben counties and runs three schools, Prairie Heights Elementary, Middle and High School {nces_ph}{ph_board}{kpc_may2026}. Federal data list 1,346 students in grades K-12 for 2024-25 {nces_ph}. Jeff Reed is superintendent {ph_home}{ph_min_20260921}.

How the board is elected: the board has five members {ph_board}, and seats are tied to townships; the two seats on the 2026 ballot are the Milford Township and Millgrove Township seats, and a 2020 race was for the Jackson Township seat {kpc_may2026}{kpc_2020}. Each 2026 race fills one seat, matching the state list's 'vote for 1' {kpc_jul2026}{in_list}. The state list labels both races '(LaGrange, Steuben)' {in_list}; this guide did not confirm whether voters across the whole district vote on each township seat. Board members are paid $2,000 a year plus $50 for committee or extra meetings {ph_min_20260121}.

Who holds the seats now: Todd Perkins holds the Milford Township seat and Jesslyn Senecal the Millgrove Township seat {kpc_jan2026}. Perkins is not on the 2026 ballot, so Milford is an open seat with four candidates {in_list}{kpc_jul2026}. Senecal was appointed to the Millgrove seat by a 4-0 board vote on June 26, 2023, after board president Brook German left the board {kpc_vacancy2023}{ph_min_20230626}. The other members are Heather Culler (president), Aaron Pfafman (vice president) and Jamie Staton {ph_board}{ph_min_20260121}.

Party labels: this is the first Indiana school board election in which candidates could declare a party {kpc_jul2026}{kpc_may2026}. In Milford, Steven Ceaglske, Jordan Henschen and Kenneth Sheets filed as Republicans and William Morr with no party; in Millgrove, Harmonee McCrea filed as a Republican and Senecal with no party {kpc_jul2026}{in_list}. KPC News noted particular interest in the Prairie Heights races, where both seats are contested {kpc_jul2026}.

Teacher and staff pay: on Nov. 6, 2025 the board voted 5-0 to ratify a 2025-27 agreement with the Prairie Heights Education Association giving certified staff a $3,500 base-pay increase in 2025-26 and $2,000 in 2026-27, plus a $2,500 stipend in each year; administrators received the same base increases {ph_min_20251106}. Classified staff received $1.50 an hour more in each year, bus drivers' daily rate rose from $109.50 to $112.50 and then $115.50, and food service employees received $1,350 stipends in each year {ph_min_20251106}. No public comments were received on the contract {ph_min_20251106}.

Budget: the board adopted the 2026 budget, Capital Projects Fund plan and Bus Replacement Plan 5-0 on Oct. 20, 2025 {ph_min_20251020}. In August 2026 it approved a resolution to reduce appropriations, and on Sept. 21, 2026 it held the public hearing on the 2027 budget, CPF plan and bus plan, presented by CFO Christine Orr {ph_min_20260817}{ph_min_20260921}. This guide found no reporting on how the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) affects Prairie Heights, and no operating or safety referendum.

Facilities: in August 2026 Reed reported bond-project work completed over the prior year: about $3.2 million at the high school (classroom ceilings and LED lighting, a press box, concession stand renovations) and about $2.0 million at the elementary and middle schools (furniture, paint, carpet, playgrounds, paving and roof work), and said a plan for summer 2027 renovations would come in the following months {ph_min_20260817}. In October 2025 the board approved a $338,447.08 furniture purchase, compared with a $443,628.25 cooperative-contract quote {ph_min_20251020}.

Safety and student support: in January 2026 the board approved hiring a corporation police officer and a part-time security receptionist {ph_min_20260121}. In September 2026 Reed reported a 2026-27 service agreement with Bowen Health for mental health services {ph_min_20260921}.

Academics: 103 of 108 Prairie Heights third graders (95.4%) passed the IREAD reading test in 2026, according to KPC News; principals also reported a 97.7% high school graduation rate in August 2026 {kpc_iread_2026}{ph_min_20260817}. A December 2025 work session covered dual credit, the Indiana College Core and new state graduation requirements {ph_min_20251215}.
Public input: board minutes for 2025-26 meetings regularly record no public comments {ph_min_20251106}{ph_min_20260921}.

Forum: Reed reminded the board of a School Board Candidate Forum on Sept. 30, 2026 at 6 p.m. in the middle school cafeteria {ph_min_20260921}. This guide found no coverage of what candidates said there.

review_flags.person: Todd Perkins (current Milford Township member; not a 2026 candidate)
review_flags.summary: A Nov. 13, 2025 letter to the editor from a district resident said that at the Nov. 6, 2025 board meeting Perkins remarked that staff were receiving pay increases while the board was 'not getting anything in return' and complained about $230,000 spent on substitute pay the prior year; the writer criticized the remarks {kpc_letter_20251113}. The official minutes of that meeting record the 5-0 contract votes but no discussion {ph_min_20251106}. No response from Perkins was found.
review_flags.note: Source is an opinion letter, not news reporting; the remarks are not confirmed by the minutes (a meeting video on the board's YouTube channel was not reviewed). Perkins is not on the ballot; relevant only as context for the open Milford seat. Likely omit.
